claims.text: Creep resistance in the FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy coating is governed by coherent interfaces between the FCC and BCC phases.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces inhibit dislocation motion.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces suppress stress-assisted diffusion.
The starting coating contains intermixed FCC and BCC regions with fine, coherent phase boundaries.
Fine coherent phase boundaries give the starting coating moderate resistance to plastic deformation under sustained stress.
Annealing or cooling-rate changes can vary FCC/BCC phase fractions and interfacial coherency while leaving overall composition unchanged.
Elevated-temperature sustained loading can produce creep in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed interface mechanism operates below the thresholds for phase instability and crack propagation and near service-limit stresses.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces impede both dislocation glide and dislocation climb during elevated-temperature loading.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces slow stress-assisted atomic diffusion along or near phase boundaries.
Interface-induced stress localization obstructs the cooperative mechanisms required for plastic flow.
A higher volume fraction of coherent FCC/BCC interfaces will lower the creep strain rate under identical load and temperature conditions.
A higher volume fraction of coherent FCC/BCC interfaces will delay the onset of plastic deformation.
A higher volume fraction of coherent FCC/BCC interfaces will improve overall creep resistance.
Standard processing produces a balanced FCC/BCC baseline with moderate interfacial coherency and typical creep behavior.
The interface-controlled mechanism ceases to govern when phase instability, cracking, or excessive-plasticity failure modes occur.
Grain-boundary sliding and diffusional creep may contribute under some operating conditions.
Coherent phase boundaries are expected to be the dominant contributor to creep resistance.
The proposed controlled comparison holds alloy composition, load, and temperature constant while varying phase constitution or interface coherency.
Failure of the high-coherency group to show a statistically significant creep-rate reduction or creep-resistance improvement relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field allows the baseline to be single-phase, whereas the baseline field explicitly defines it as a balanced dual-phase FCC/BCC coating with moderate coherency.
